en: Puggalapaññatti Niddesa 6. Exposition of the Sixfold Designation of Persons

In this regard, that person who, regarding teachings never heard before, personally awakens to the Truths and therein attains omniscience and mastery over the powers, should be regarded as a Perfectly Enlightened One (Sammāsambuddha).

In this regard, that person who, regarding teachings never heard before, personally awakens to the Truths but does not therein attain omniscience nor mastery over the powers, should be regarded as a Solitary Buddha (Paccekasambuddha).
In this regard, that person who, regarding teachings unheard before,
personally awakens to the Truths and, in this very life, makes an end of suffering, attaining the perfection of a disciple— he should be seen as Sāriputta and Moggallāna.
In this regard, that person who, regarding teachings unheard before, personally awakens to the Truths...
One who puts an end to suffering in this very life, yet does not reach the perfection of a disciple— such a person should be seen as an arahant of the remaining type.
In that regard, the person who, regarding teachings unheard before, personally awakens to the truths by himself, but does not put an end to suffering in this very life,
and is a non-returner who does not come back to this state of being— that person should be seen as a non-returner.
In this regard, that person who, regarding teachings not heard before,
personally awakens to the Truths but does not make an end of suffering in this very life, and returns to this state of existence— this refers to the stream-enterer and the once-returner.
This is the Exposition of the Sixfold Set.
